assistant_message.content: I'll compute k_r using the Strickler-Berg formula directly.

arguments.summary:
I computed the radiative rate constant k_r for the S1 → S0 transition of anthracene using the Strickler-Berg formula with the published parameters provided (E(S1) = 3.43 eV, f = 0.10, n = 1.0, T = 298 K).

**Result: k_r ≈ 5.18 × 10⁷ s⁻¹** (radiative lifetime τ_r ≈ 19.3 ns)

This is in excellent agreement with both reference values: it sits essentially on top of the Niu/Shuai 2008 TVCF computed value of 5.2 × 10⁷ s⁻¹ (within ~0.4%), and is within ~15% of the Berlman 1971 experimental value of 4.5 × 10⁷ s⁻¹ — well within the expected accuracy of the Strickler-Berg approximation, which assumes a mirror-image absorption/emission relationship and uses the vertical (not 0-0) energy. No chemistry decisions were required since all inputs were specified by the user; the formula was applied directly via the photophysics KB module.
